messages:
From: Elaine Rivera <elaine.rivera@somamed.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@somamed.com
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 08:24:00 -0800
Subject: DPA follow-up: model improvement & exportability

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the review call this morning. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of concrete asks so their legal team can sign off quickly: 

- We need an explicit "no adaptive training / no-model-improvement" commitment for tenant interactions that are tagged as PHI or PII.
- Clarify whether "no-train" also prevents any derivative indexing or synthetic dataset generation. Procurement uses the term "no-derive" and they'd like the contract language to map to that concept.
- Can you confirm if Redwood will provide a subprocessors inventory and attestations for KMS location (onshore/US-only) for any customer keys?
- Finally, exportability: we need a clear path to export our conversation transcripts and associated outputs (for e-discovery). Are there standard export formats and SLA for export availability?

I'm attaching the redlines we started and the procurement checklist. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Elaine Rivera
Head of Product & Data Privacy — SomaMed
elaine.rivera@somamed.com

Attachments: SomaMed_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf, evidence-checklist.xlsx

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Rivera <elaine.rivera@somamed.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: model improvement & exportability

Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list and the redlines. Short answers up front and then operational asks below: 

- No-training: Redwood can commit to "no adaptive training" (we will not use customer interactions to update model weights or create derivative training datasets) for the SomaMed tenant by default once the no-train toggle is enabled for your account.
- No-derive vs no-train: We distinguish between "no-train" (no weight updates / model retraining) and "no-derive" (no creation of derivative datasets or synthetic data derived from your data). We can add a narrow "no-derive" clause to the DPA/Amendment if that better captures procurement's needs — we'll route to legal for precise language.
- Subprocessors & KMS: We maintain a subprocessors inventory and can provide a time-stamped snapshot. For customer-managed keys (BYOK), we support KMS integrations with onshore-cloud providers; we can provide an attestation of key residency for the keys you use.
- Exports: We support transcript export via API (JSONL, CSV) and SFTP dump for larger exports; typical export SLA is 48 hours for >50GB requests, 24 hours for smaller requests. We can discuss tightening for DocuSign/purchase-order-driven needs.

Operational next steps (cc'ing David and Jordan):
- David: can you confirm the evidence pack we can provide for KMS residency + subprocessors snapshot and an estimated turnaround?
- Jordan: procurement timeline — if SomaMed wants a DPA amendment with "no-derive" language, can you estimate legal review time and whether we need an SLA exception?

I can hop on a call late Monday afternoon PT if that helps move things faster.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
(Attachments referenced: SomaMed_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf)

From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: model improvement & exportability

Thanks Vanessa / Elaine —

Quick operational clarification from privacy/ops: 

- Evidence pack: we can produce a signed attestation that for the SomaMed tenant (tenant id SOMA-4581) the platform will not use customer inputs for model weight updates when the tenancy-level "no-train" toggle is set. Attestation will include a timestamped subprocessors snapshot (list + roles) and the KMS integration type used (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed). Estimated delivery: 5 business days once we receive a signed amendment request.

- KMS residency: if SomaMed provides keys via a supported BYOK provider, we can confirm key wrapping and that plaintext never leaves the onshore provider. For Redwood-managed keys we can provide region residency statements and SOC2 evidence for our cloud kms provider. Need to know whether SomaMed requires HSM-backed attestations or a specific provider name.

- No-derive clause: legal should review exact clause, but operationally we can implement technical controls to mark transcripts as "non-derivable" for downstream analytics pipelines (no indexing, no embeddings, no synthetic generation). Note: some downstream platform features (search indexing, analytics) will need to be disabled for those datasets — we should surface impacts to product managers.

Action items: 
1) SomaMed: confirm whether you will use BYOK (customer KMS) or require Redwood to manage keys.
2) SomaMed procurement: attach the signed amendment template or indicate which redline items are blockers.
3) Vanessa/Jordan: coordinate legal redline turnaround and whether we need an SLA exception for export speed.

--
David Kim
Director, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.ai
